candidates.title: Final ViaSat-3 Satellite Enters Service, Completing High-Capacity Trio
candidates.raw_excerpt: The final ViaSat-3 satellite entered service late last week, completing deployment of Viasat’s high-capacity satellite trio. This satellite, ViaSat-3 F2, was actually the second satellite to launch, and it launched in November of last year . All three satellites are now in service and the ViaSat-3 constellation is fully operational after the F3 satellite entered service about a month ago in late August . The F3 satellite covers the Asia-Pacific region and F2 covers the Americas. Each satellite adds more than 1 terabit per second of capacity to Viasat’s network to bolster its business in aviation, maritime, government, and broadband. The F1 satellite, which launched in 2023, suffered an anomaly with its antenna deployment. That satellite is operational, but only delivering a fraction of the capacity that was expected. Beyond the capacity, the satellites are equipped with beamforming technology to allocate beams based on the location of demand, which Viasat sees as a critical differentiator. “We believe that the VS3 satellites are the most advanced commercial satellites in the world in terms of adaptive beam forming for cost efficiencies, user performance improvements that offer higher speeds on both forward and return links, and resilience to interference,” Viasat CEO Mark Dankberg said in a statement. “We also believe VS3 technology sets new commercial standards for solar power generation and thermal dissipation – both critical technology challenges for developing economical data centers in space.” The post Final ViaSat-3 Satellite Enters Service, Completing High-Capacity Trio appeared first on Via Satellite .

candidates.title: Intellian to Develop Multi-Band WGS Terminals With Network Innovations
candidates.raw_excerpt: Intellian Technologies and Network Innovations plan to jointly develop and distribute multi-band Wideband Global Satcom (WGS) flyaway terminals for military and government customers under a new strategic partnership announced last week. This will be Intellian’s first tactical ground WGS flyaway platform. Intellian said these terminals are set to be the first to support simultaneous Mil-X, Mil Ka-band and commercial Ka- and Ku-band connectivity. The platform is designed for multi-band and multi-orbit operations across Low-Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO), Geostationary Orbit (GEO), and Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO), as well as interoperability with emerging satellite networks. Network Innovations provides managed network services and system integration and has an established military and government market presence. The two companies have worked together for many years and this is a new multi-year agreement to expand their relationship. Intellian CEO Eric Sung said it marks an expansion of the company’s military-government portfolio. “By combining simultaneous X-band and Military Ka-band capability, access to wider commercial Ka frequencies, and multi-orbit connectivity in a rapidly deployable architecture, we are addressing the increasingly complex communications requirements of modern defense operations. Our goal is to give operators greater flexibility, resilience, and assured connectivity wherever their missions take them,” Sung said in a release. In March, Intellian previewed it would be moving into WGS flyaway terminals during SATShow Week. Flyaway terminals are meant to be rapidly deployable for forces in the field, to be set up in less than 30 minutes. Intellian also said it plans to expand the platform for government, enterprise, and critical communications applications outside of military. candidates.title: Katalyst to Demo Space-Based Power Beaming for Pentagon Energy Investment Program
candidates.raw_excerpt: Katalyst Space has been selected by a Pentagon energy investment program to take part in a space-based power beaming to remote locations, working with the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory (NRL). Under the Advanced Scalable Growth Architecture for Robotic Deployment (ASGARD) program, Katalyst will develop and launch a robotic spacecraft that will assemble a large-format power beaming system on orbit and transmit power back to Earth, the company announced Monday. Katalyst was selected by the Operational Energy Capability Improvement Fund (OECIF), which issues awards focused on maturing first-of-its-kind energy technologies for future warfighting platforms. Quantum space also recently received an OECIF award . The NRL is developing modular tiles to form a large-format power beaming system. In the ASGARD mission, a Katalyst Nexus spacecraft will use robotic arms to assemble the tiles on-orbit to create the power beaming system. The tiles will then harness solar energy, convert it to radio frequency microwave energy, and transmit that energy down to Earth. Katalyst recently had tech issues with a servicing spacecraft launched to rescue NASA’s Swift Observatory. The company has also recently won a Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) contract for a deorbit-as-a-service program . Katalyst highlighted how its Nexus spacecraft is able to serve multiple types of missions. “This important, first-of-a-kind technology opens new pathways for operational energy in space,” Director of Operational Energy – Innovation RuthAnne Darling said. “Demonstrating this groundbreaking technology, autonomously assembling large-scale power and energy collectors in space, is the first step and a foundational one.” The post Katalyst to Demo Space-Based Power Beaming for Pentagon Energy Investment Program appeared first on Via Satellite .

Several possible explanations have since emerged, with some arguing they could be emerging galaxies. They found that the rapidly-forming black holes could be emitting light while accreting material, appearing as the mysterious red dots, or “seeds,” picked up by the James Webb. Despite lurking pretty much everywhere we look in our known universe, the nature of black holes remains mysterious. candidates.title: China advances lunar spacesuit, bed rest research for moon landing
candidates.raw_excerpt:
China has advanced its push for a crewed moon landing by 2030, with its lunar spacesuit and a bed rest experiment for long-term space stays both progressing, the country's astronaut center said on Saturday.

The development of China's moon-landing spacesuit Wangyu, meaning "gazing into the cosmos," is progressing smoothly, with dozens of key technologies now in place, said Zhang Wanxin, an expert at the Astronaut Center of China, at an aerospace medical engineering conference in north China's Tianjin.

Since development began in 2020, efforts on Wangyu have focused on meeting the demands of complex lunar-surface operations and extreme environmental challenges, Zhang said, noting that the lunar spacesuit is designed to be lightweight, miniaturized, highly efficient and safe.

Beyond spacesuit development, China is also advancing astronaut health research, having completed the "Dixing-3" bed rest experiment to address physiological protection challenges associated with long-term space stays and crewed lunar landing missions.

According to Qu Lina, a center expert, the experiment began in May this year. Volunteers were divided into different groups and spent 15 or 30 days in bed. During the experiment, they completed daily activities such as eating, washing, sleeping, urinating and defecating while lying in bed.

Results showed that the experiment effectively protects the human bone, muscle and cardiovascular systems, and it will provide technical support for long-term space stays and crewed lunar landing missions.

candidates.raw_excerpt:
US President Donald Trump said Saturday that he is forming an "AI Force" and will announce an "AI Czar" in the near future.

In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump said he would not stand by and let the "decimation or destruction" of AI happen.

"We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," Trump said.

Trump also described AI as the next Industrial Revolution or Internet, and said it could possibly account for as much as 25% of US gross domestic product.

Trump did not provide details on the structure of the planned "AI Force" or the role of the "AI Czar."

The announcement comes amid growing debate in the United States over the rapid development of AI and its potential risks.
